hook: Google's email system was about to get a radical makeover in 2004.
body: Back then, Gmail felt like it had everything covered—until Google engineer Aaron Swartz introduced the Inbox by Gmail. This new interface focused on organizing emails into folders based on conversations rather than dates or subjects. It was simple but revolutionary because it made navigation intuitive and saved users from endless thread scrolling. By 2016, this feature had grown to handle over 5 billion messages a day, transforming email management for millions worldwide.
